chunks: From him, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Muyassir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"The deception (or overcharging) of a believer is forbidden."

key_terms.غَبْنُ: Deception or overcharging in trade, specifically charging more than the worth or hiding defects.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on deceiving a believer in trade according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In the context of Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this concise narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) underscores the spiritual sanctity of the believer’s rights in commerce, linking economic integrity to faith. It serves as a foundational legal maxim in Shia jurisprudence, prohibiting *ghabn* (deception or unfair advantage) not merely as a civil breach but as a religious violation that erodes communal trust. This principle is often cited alongside the prohibition of *riba* (usury) to highlight that honesty is as obligatory as avoiding interest in Islamic trade ethics.
